definition: Callous means coldly unfeeling toward the suffering of others.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word callous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know callous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Mocking the rookie's stage fright in front of the whole cast was callous, the director said, and she benched the veteran actor for a week.
Uncaring is milder than callous — uncaring simply fails to notice, while callous notices suffering and remains unmoved by it.
Cruel goes further than callous — the callous boss ignores your pain, while the cruel one inflicts it.

Heartless is the blunter, more damning accusation — no pity anywhere, as if the organ were missing. Callous is more specific about the mechanism: feeling worn hard, like a callus, so that another person's suffering no longer gets through. A heartless villain never had warmth; a callous one has stopped letting pain in.

Unfeeling names a flat, passive absence of sympathy — a temperament with the warmth switched off. Callous is more pointed and more active: a callous person sees particular suffering in front of them and stays hard toward it. Unfeeling describes what someone lacks; callous describes how they treat pain they witnessed.

Use 'insensitive' for mere social clumsiness and save callous for indifference that wounds — a callous remark, a callous policy.
It attaches naturally to acts and decisions rather than to looks or moods.
